chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Malik ibn Atiyya, from Minhal al-Qassab, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever recites the Quran and he is a young believer, the Quran blends with his flesh and his blood, and God Mighty and Majestic places him with the honourable, righteous scribes [angels]. And the Quran will be a defender for him on the Day of Resurrection, saying: 'O my Lord! Every worker has received the reward of his deeds except my [faithful] doer — so let him reach the most prestigious of Your gifts.'

He said: 'Then God, the Mighty and Compeller, will clothe him with two garments from the garments of Paradise and place a crown of honour upon his head. Then it is said to him [the Quran]: Have We pleased you regarding him?' So the Quran says: 'O my Lord! I used to wish for him that which is superior to this.' So he is given security in his right hand and eternity in his left. Then he enters Paradise, and it is said to him: 'Recite and ascend a level.' Then it is said to him: 'Have We made him reach it and pleased you?' And he [the Quran] says: 'Yes.'
He said: 'And whoever recites it frequently and regularly reviews it with difficulty — from the intensity of memorizing it — God Mighty and Majestic will give him the reward of this twice.'

key_terms.الأَمْن وَالخُلْد: Security and eternity — the two deeds placed in the believer's hands, representing freedom from fear and everlasting life
key_terms.السَّفَرَة الكِرَام البَرَرَة: The honourable, righteous scribes — interpreted in the Quran (80:15-16) as the noble recording angels; association with them is a mark of spiritual excellence
key_terms.تَاج الكَرَامَة: Crown of honour — a reward imagery reflecting the elevated status of Quran bearers in Paradise
key_terms.حَجِيز: Barrier, defender, or intercessor — the Quran acting as a shield/advocate for its reciter before God on Judgment Day
key_terms.مَشَقَّة: Difficulty, hardship — the struggle of memorization which doubles one's reward according to this teaching

ai.seo_question: What reward does a young believer receive for reciting the Quran according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) describes the extraordinary eschatological rewards awaiting the young believing Quran reciter: the Quran becomes part of his very flesh and blood in this life, then on the Day of Judgment it intercedes for him as an advocate before God, asking for the most precious gifts. The believer receives two robes of Paradise, a crown of honour, and deeds of security and eternity placed in his hands. The hadith reflects early Shia theological understanding that deep Quranic recitation — especially in youth when habits form — creates a spiritual bond between the reciter and scripture that persists into the next world. The closing teaching that those who struggle with memorization receive double reward demonstrates the Imam's compassionate pedagogy and encouragement for those who find Quran learning difficult.
